About the Report
Forward to Readers
Torrent Power Limited ('Torrent Power', 
'The Company', or 'We') proudly 
presents its fifth Integrated Annual 
Report for FY26. This Report provides 
a transparent and holistic view of 
our performance, governance, and 
impact across both financial and 
non-financial dimensions. We invite 
our stakeholders to engage with us as 
we continue to power a smarter, more 
resilient tomorrow.
Frameworks, Guidelines, 
and Standards
Our Report is prepared in adherence 
to globally recognised frameworks and 
standards to ensure transparency, 
accountability, and comparability. It 
aligns with:
• Integrated Reporting (IR) 
Framework  – Developed by the 
International Integrated Reporting 
Council (IIRC), now part of the 
IFRS Foundation
• Global Reporting Initiative (GRI)  
–  Key sustainability performance 
metrics mapped to GRI Standards
• Sustainability Accounting 
Standards Board (SASB)
• United Nations Sustainable 
Development Goals (UN SDGs)
• United Nations Global Compact 
(UNGC)
• National Guidelines for 
Responsible Business Conduct 
(NGRBC)Regulatory Compliance
This report meets statutory 
requirements in accordance with:
• Companies Act, 2013 (including 
applicable rules)
• Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
• SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015
• Secretarial Standards issued 
by the Institute of Company 
Secretaries of India
Reporting Period, 
Boundary and Scope
• Period Covered: April 1, 2025, to 
March 31, 2026
• Boundary & Scope: Our disclosures 
provide a comprehensive view of 
operations of Torrent Power and 
it's Subsidiaries across:
 − Thermal Generation
 − Renewable Generation
 − Licensed Distribution
 −Franchised Distribution
 − Transmission
Integrated Thinking 
At Torrent Power, integrated 
thinking shapes how we plan, 
operate and deliver outcomes. We 
recognise that long-term growth 
depends on maintaining strong and 
responsible relationships with our 
key stakeholders—capital providers, 
employees, suppliers, customers, 
communities and the environment.
Every strategic decision is therefore 
guided by the need to balance 
diverse stakeholder expectations 
while managing opportunities and 
potential trade-offs. This approach 
enables us to strengthen trust, maintain operational resilience and 
create sustainable outcomes across 
our ecosystem.
By embedding ESG considerations into 
our operations and aligning our efforts 
with the United Nations Sustainable 
Development Goals (SDGs), we 
continue to support India 's energy 
transition while delivering reliable and 
responsible power solutions.
Responsibility Statement
Our Board of Directors affirms the 
integrity, balance, and completeness 
of this Report, ensuring alignment 
with the principles of the Integrated 
Reporting Framework.

www.torrentpower.comAbout Torrent Power
Torrent Power is among India 's leading integrated 
power utilities, serving ~4.3 million customers and 
having a  footprint across 10 states and 1 Union 
Territory, with operations spanning the entire energy 
value chain. Supported by a balanced portfolio of 
clean renewable capacity and efficient thermal 
generation, along with advanced transmission 
networks and customer-centric distribution systems, 
we deliver electricity that is reliable, affordable and 
sustainable.

Building Core Strength  
Unlocking Future Potential
 
FY 2025–26 marks a pivotal phase in our evolution where 
operational resilience meets forward-looking ambition. As India 's 
energy landscape undergoes a profound transformation, we are 
strengthening our core foundations while advancing a growth 
strategy aligned to the long-term trajectory of the energy transition.
2

=== page 7 ===
Building Core Strength
Our integrated business model 
spanning generation, distribution, 
and transmission provides the scale, 
diversification, and resilience required 
to serve India 's energy needs reliably 
across cycles. Our thermal generation 
fleet is uniquely positioned to meet 
immediate power deficits with speed 
and flexibility, while our distribution 
business consistently delivers high-
quality power to some of India 's most 
economically vibrant regions. The 
addition of a 1.6 GW coal-based power 
plant will  further strengthen our 
ability to provide dependable baseload 
capacity, supporting the needs of a 
rapidly industrialising economy.Unlocking Future Potential
We are accelerating India 's transition 
to clean, secure, and accessible 
energy with the scale and conviction 
this moment demands. Our ~4 GW 
renewable pipeline spanning wind, 
solar, hybrid, and firm-and-dispatchable 
solutions is actively under execution. 
Our 3 GW pumped storage portfolio, 
currently under construction, is 
expected to support grid-scale energy 
storage and enable more reliable 
integration of renewable energy. With 
an ambition to build 10 GW of renewable 
capacity by 2030, we are not just 
participating in India 's energy transition, 
we are shaping its trajectory.

Introducing our 
New Identity
For over half a century, T orrent has 
grown steadily across sectors critical 
to society—power, pharmaceuticals 
and gas. This growth has been 
shaped not by short-term ambition, 
but by discipline, integrity, and a long-
term view of progress.
At every stage, Torrent has focused on building 
scale with stability—strengthening foundations 
before expanding horizons. That philosophy 
continues to define how we operate, invest, 
and evolve.
As the organisation has grown in size, complexity, 
and responsibility, the need emerged for an 
identity that reflects this maturity, one that 
represents both the strength of what has been 
built and the momentum of what lies ahead.
Our new logo is a considered  
evolution of that thinking.
It draws from the strength of our foundation - 
stable, balanced, and resilient, while adopting 
a more refined and contemporary form that 
reflects adaptability and forward momentum. 
The design is a balance between being solid 
and dependable, and agile and future-ready. 
The identity mirrors how Torrent operates 
today: grounded in values, yet responsive to a 
changing world.
This  evolution is not a shift in 
direction. It is a clearer articulation 
of who we are and how we will 
continue to build for the future.

Core Values
When truth  
is paramount
Thoughts and actions entail doing 
the right thing at all times and in all 
circumstances, whether or not anyone 
is watching. This requires inner courage 
and conviction, no matter what the 
consequences are. It is honouring one 's 
commitments and being accountable 
for one's actions, end-to-end.
When every smile 
matters
Concern for Society and Environment is a 
sense of responsibility and contribution 
to society that defines our existence. It 
entails making a difference in the quality 
of lives and environment surrounding 
us. It is important to encourage fellow 
members on collective as well as 
individual basis to fulfil the responsibility 
of leaving behind a world rich in flora and 
fauna and rich in time tested values and 
ideals and, above all, rich in social fervour 
for our future generations. When best  
is not enough
Passion for excellence means not doing 
extraordinary things, but doing ordinary 
things in all pursuits exceedingly well. 
Passion and excellence are forces 
that fuel each other on the exclusive 
path to leadership. As we are what we 
repeatedly do, excellence then is not an 
act, but a habit.
Harnessing equality
Fairness and Care towards all fellow 
members are inextricably linked. 
Weaving the threads of equality, 
irrespective of caste, creed, religion, 
and gender, into the day-to-day fabric, 
ensures fairness for each and every 
individual. Empathic care recognises 
the needs and aspirations of all. Only 
such fairness and care eventually 
lead fellow members to the dawn of 
eternal success.Involvement that  
engenders effectiveness
An ideal organisation facilitates 
participation and involvement of each 
of its members in various decision-
making processes, thus ensuring 
their commitment to such decisions 
as well as its outcome. It provides a 
platform for seeking and nurturing 
constructive ideas from individuals, 
teams, and units which eventually 
yields exceptional results.
Openness that  
builds enduring trust
Transparency implies openness. It is 
the opposite of secrecy. It encourages 
more informed decision-making and 
aids in creating enduring trust among 
all stakeholders.Integrity

Dear Stakeholders,
FY26 was a transformative year of 
growth and expansion. We increased 
our thermal power capacity through 
a mix of greenfield and brownfield 
investments. Our clean energy 
portfolio also continued to grow 
steadily with new renewable energy 
additions. These developments are 
aligned with India 's vision of energy 
independence by 2047 and Net Zero 
emissions by 2070. Throughout the 
year, we remained committed to 
strengthening our core capabilities 
while actively pursuing opportunities 
across the coal, renewable, and green 
energy segments to drive future 
growth. Our performance reflects 
operational excellence, underpinned 
by disciplined capital allocation, 
strategic investments, robust network 
expansion, and strengthened fuel 
security. Together, these initiatives 
reinforce our long-term vision of being 
a trusted partner in India 's energy 
security journey. I am pleased to share 
our progress and outline our vision for 
sustainable growth in the years ahead.
A Transforming Energy 
Landscape
The evolution of India's power 
landscape has reached an inflection 
point, as urbanisation, rural 
electrification, digital infrastructure 
expansion, rising cooling demands, 
and clean energy innovations place 
unprecedented pressure on the grid. 
Peak demand is expected to increase 
from ~245 GW in FY26 to ~459 GW 
by FY36, and total energy demand is 
expected to rise at a CAGR of above 
6% to 3,365 billion units. Installed 
capacity will need to scale up to ~1,121 
GW, with ~786 GW expected to come 
from non-fossil sources. This growth 
will require accelerated investments 
in renewable energy, thermal power, 
storage solutions, and transmission infrastructure to ensure grid stability 
and efficient energy evacuation. 
India's power sector achieved several 
significant milestones during the 
year, including the addition of ~65 GW 
of generation capacity and the 
attainment of the NDC (Nationally 
Determined Contribution) target of 
50% cumulative non-fossil fuel-based 
installed electricity capacity, nearly 
five years ahead of schedule. These 
achievements, along with key initiatives 
such as the SHANTI Act 2025, and the 
PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, marked 
the country's transition from a power-
deficient to a power-surplus nation.
Notwithstanding the dynamic 
environment of the Indian power 
sector, our operations are guided by 
a strong focus on building long-term 
capabilities, capitalising on emerging 
opportunities to enhance performance 
and create value for our stakeholders. 
With our presence across generation, 
transmission, and distribution, we are  
well-positioned to respond effectively 
to the transforming energy landscape. 
The year reaffirmed the strength of 
our strategy and the confidence our 
stakeholders place in us.
Financial and Operational 
Performance
Torrent Power delivered a strong 
performance across its generation, 
transmission, and distribution 
businesses in FY26, reinforcing its 
ability to unlock sustained growth 
through disciplined execution, 
strategic investments, and alignment 
with India 's energy transition goals. The 
Company 's total generation capacity, 
including projects under construction, 
stood at ~10,644 MWp, of which 
renewable energy capacity accounted 
for ~5,952 MWp, representing ~56% of 
the total portfolio.
Thermal generation remains a critical 
pillar of the nation 's energy security, in alignment with which we continue 
to strengthen our presence in this 
segment through a disciplined and 
strategic approach. During the year, we 
signed a long-term PPA with MPPMCL 
for a 1,600 MW ultra-supercritical 
coal-based power plant in Anuppur, 
Madhya Pradesh, and secured access 
to ~922 acres of strategically located 
land near coal sources. 
We also entered into a definitive 
agreement with Larsen & Toubro 
Ltd. (L&T) for the acquisition of its 
1,400 MW Nabha Power Limited 
(NPL). This is underpinned by a 
long-term PPA with Punjab State 
Power Corporation Limited, ensuring 
stable and predictable cash flows, 
and benefits from assured fuel linkage 
through subsidiaries of Coal India. 
Equipped with advanced supercritical 
technology, the plant is designed to 
deliver high operational efficiency, with 
availability exceeding 90%.
We also made steady progress in 
expanding our renewable portfolio 
during the year. Torrent Green Energy 
Private Limited (a wholly owned 
subsidiary of Torrent Power Limited) 
secured a Letter of Award for a 300 MW 
wind project under SECI' s Wind 
Tranche-XVIII at a tariff of ₹3.97 per unit, 
along with a 250 MW FDRE project from 
our own DISCOM at ₹4.87 per kWh. 
We also commissioned ~227 MWp 
of solar capacity under the MSKVY 
programme, along with ~29 MWp of C&I 
capacity. In addition, we added a gross 
of ~549 MWp of solar and 503 MW of 
wind capacity under construction, 
taking our total installed renewable 
energy capacity to ~2 GWp, with nearly 
4 GWp under development.
We are also exploring pumped hydro 
storage opportunities in Maharashtra 
and Uttar Pradesh to enhance grid 
flexibility and ensure reliable renewable 
power delivery, with a cumulative 
potential capacity of around 8.4 GW. 
Of this, we are developing 3 GW of

Message from the Chairman
storage capacity, including 2 GW 
already secured under firm 40-year 
agreements with the Maharashtra 
State Electricity Distribution Company 
Limited (MSEDCL). The project entails a 
planned investment of around ₹14,000 
Crore and is positioned as India 's 
largest pumped storage initiative. In 
parallel, we strengthened our future 
energy platform with the inauguration 
of our first green hydrogen plant at 
Gorakhpur for blending into the CGD 
network, with an annual capacity of 
72 tonnes TPA, developed jointly by 
Torrent Power and Torrent Gas.
On our gas-based portfolio, the 
Company actively participated in the 
merchant market, including NVVN 
tenders and Section 11 opportunities. 
Strengthening our fuel security and 
risk management framework, we 
executed long-term LNG procurement 
agreements with BP and JERA, securing 
~10 cargoes annually (including for our 
group company) over a 10-year period 
commencing April 2027.
Our distribution business continued 
to deliver benchmark operational 
efficiency, achieving distribution losses 
of ~2.33% in licensed distribution 
areas, among the lowest in the country 
and at par with global best practices, 
serving ~4.3 million customers across 
three states and one Union Territory. 
This exceptional performance has 
been widely recognised, with our 
Ahmedabad and Surat distribution 
circles securing the 1st rank (with 
100/100 score and A+ grade) in the 
national utility rankings among 65 
discoms in the 14th Integrated Ratings 
and Rankings released by the Ministry 
of Power in January 2026. Further 
underscoring our commitment to 
quality and continuous improvement, 
our Ahmedabad, Surat, and Dahej 
distribution units have achieved 
a historic milestone by becoming 
the first and only organisation in 
India to be awarded 6 Diamonds under the prestigious EFQM Global 
Award framework.
In our franchised distribution areas, 
Agra stands out as a noteworthy 
success story, where Aggregate 
Technical & Commercial (AT&C) losses 
have been brought down to a record 
low of 5.36% this year, a remarkable 
turnaround from the 58.77% at the 
time of takeover in 2010, highlighting 
our long-term commitment to 
system reliability, loss reduction, and 
customer-centric service delivery.
Torrent Power Grid Limited (TPGL), 
a subsidiary of the Company, 
achieved a key milestone with the 
successful commissioning of its 
transmission project in February 2026 
to evacuate 4.5 GW of renewable 
power from Khavda, Gujarat. The 
project, comprising 60 km of 
400 kV multi- circuit transmission 
lines along with associated bay 
upgrades, underscores our execution 
capabilities and unwavering focus on 
strengthening renewable integration. 
The Company reported a Profit 
Before Tax (PBT) of ₹3,317 Crore for 
the FY26, remaining stable year-on-
year, supported by strong operating 
performance in the distribution 
business. This was driven by a 
continued reduction in distribution 
losses, additional incentives improving 
Return on Equity (RoE) under the 
revised regulations implemented from 
April 1, 2025, and from incremental 
capital expenditure during the year. 
Performance further improved with 
the contribution from renewables on 
account of a higher plant load factor. 
This was partially offset by lower 
merchant sales from gas-based power 
plants, including RLNG sales. Overall, 
the Company 's operating performance 
improved during the year.
During the year, capital expenditure 
totalled ₹8,681 Crore, strategically 
allocated to the improvement of 
existing networks in our distribution areas, expansion of renewable 
businesses and thermal projects. 
This underscores our continued 
emphasis on expanding coal 
and renewable energy capacity, 
strengthening transmission systems, 
and modernising distribution networks, 
thus re-enforcing our commitment 
to a sustainable energy future. We 
continue to maintain a conservative 
capital structure, strong liquidity, 
and a clear focus on cost efficiency. 
Margin stability was ensured through 
disciplined project execution, digital 
adoption, and reliable cash flows from 
regulated operations.
Building the Next 
Growth Platform
As demand grows and grid complexity 
increases, thermal power is poised 
to play a strategic role in ensuring 
energy security, resource adequacy, 
and system flexibility. Keeping this in 
mind, we are actively prioritising coal-
based generation and have planned 
significant investments in the segment 
by pursuing both organic and inorganic 
opportunities across both greenfield 
and brownfield projects. We are also 
actively participating in competitive 
bidding processes for thermal capacity 
additions, reflecting our long-term 
commitment to strengthening 
coal-based assets within the evolving 
energy landscape.
Alongside a strong focus on 
coal-based generation, our renewable 
energy portfolio remains robust 
and strategically diversified. We are 
committed to building a presence 
across the renewable energy value 
chain through participation in 
utility-scale solar and wind projects, 
hybrid solutions including firm and 
dispatchable renewable energy 
(FDRE), as well as supplying renewable 
power to commercial and industrial 
customers. We continue to evaluate 
opportunities across both greenfield 
12

=== page 17 ===
and brownfield projects to support 
scalable and sustainable growth.
Further reinforcing our long -term 
dedication to sustainable energy, 
the Company is actively working on 
emerging green energy avenues. 
These range from Pumped Hydro 
Storage to Green Hydrogen, and Green 
Ammonia. We are also implementing 
Battery Energy Storage as a part of our 
hybrid solution. These are expected 
to complement our generation 
portfolio, enhance system flexibility, 
and position us to participate 
meaningfully in the evolving low -carbon 
energy ecosystem.
On the distribution front, we continue 
to enhance customer experience 
through improved reliability and 
reduced distribution losses, which 
remains one of our core strengths. 
We are leveraging our demonstrated 
expertise in distribution operations 
to generate tangible value through 
investments in upgrading the quality of 
our network, which in turn will cultivate 
greater future potential. Alongside 
which, expansion plans through 
pursuing new distribution privatisation 
and franchisee opportunities remain 
under active consideration. We 
also plan to continue participating 
in competitive bidding processes 
for both inter-state and intra-state 
transmission projects. 
Along with these opportunities, we 
remain steadfast in our objective 
to upholding the highest standards 
of ESG performance. Sustainability, 
transparency and responsible 
stewardship continue to guide our

Strategies in Context
The energy sector is undergoing rapid transformation, driven by the shift towards cleaner generation and storage 
solutions, increasing digitalisation of networks, and rising stakeholder expectations. For us, these changes 
translate into clear and measurable priorities: accelerating the expansion of renewable energy, modernising and 
strengthening grid infrastructure, enhancing customer experience, deepening our contribution to communities, 
and embedding sustainability across the enterprise.
Our five strategic priorities are designed to respond directly to these evolving dynamics while balancing the 
interests of customers, employees, investors, partners, regulators, and communities. Together, they provide a 
structured pathway for long-term value creation, ensuring resilience, relevance, and responsible growth as India 's 
energy ecosystem continues to evolve.

Generation Business
Our generation portfolio comprises 
a diversified mix of natural gas, 
coal, solar, and wind-based plants.

our commitment to sustainable

carbon intensity while supporting 
grid stability and reliable power for 
industrial and commercial growth.

relative to conventional coal-based

(%)Ultra Supercritical Coal Based Thermal Power 
Project (Madhya Pradesh)
We are developing a 1,600 MW  
(2 × 800 MW) ultra supercritical 
coal based thermal power 
project in Madhya Pradesh, 
representing our most 
significant greenfield thermal 
capacity addition. The project 
is being implemented under a 
Design, Build, Finance, Own and 
Operate (DBFOO) framework 
and is anchored by a long-term 
Power Purchase Agreement 
with MP Power Management 
Company Limited, with a tariff of 
₹5.829/KWh discovered through 
a competitive bidding process. 
Coal supply is secured under the 
SHAKTI policy of the Ministry of 
Coal, providing long-term fuel 
assurance.
The project is designed to 
address baseload power 
requirements while incorporating 
ultra supercritical technology, 
which offers higher thermal 
efficiency and lower emissions 
per unit of electricity compared 
to conventional subcritical plants. 
This positions the asset to deliver 
reliable, cost-competitive power 
with improved environmental 
performance, aligned with 
evolving regulatory and 
sustainability expectations.
To strengthen execution 
readiness and secure critical 
infrastructure, we undertook a 
strategic acquisition resulting 
in effective 100% ownership 
of Newzone India Private 
Limited (NZIPL). This acquisition 
provides access to 922 acres 
of strategically located land in 
the Anuppur district of Madhya 
Pradesh, with proximity to coal mines. The transaction 
significantly de-risks land 
availability, logistics planning, and 
long-term capacity development 
for the project.
Project execution has advanced 
meaningfully with the award of 
key Boiler, Turbine, Generator 
(BTG) and Balance of Plant (BoP) 
contracts. These milestones 
reinforce execution certainty 
and reflect strong project 
management capabilities. The 
Scheduled Commercial Operation 
Dates are targeted at 66 months 
and 72 months from Power 
Purchase Agreement execution 
for Unit I and Unit II, respectively.
This ultra supercritical project 
underscores our disciplined 
approach to thermal capacity 
development—combining fuel 
security, long-term offtake 
visibility, advanced technology, 
and secured infrastructure. The 
asset is expected to enhance 
portfolio resilience, support 
grid stability, and contribute 
to sustainable long-term value 
creation.

Decentralising CBM for Asset Reliability
To enhance asset reliability and 
improve field-level responsiveness, 
we decentralised Distribution 
Substation (DSS) Condition Based 
Maintenance (CBM) and Oil Quality 
Monitoring (OQM) execution to 
zonal teams in Ahmedabad. Building 
on the structured CBM programme 
introduced in FY16, this initiative 
marked a strategic shift from a 
centralised model to one driven 
by field ownership, supported 
by training, cross-functional 
collaboration and multiskilling.
The decentralised framework 
continues to leverage condition 
monitoring, thermographic inspections, earth resistance 
measurements and transformer oil 
quality analysis. Upon approval in 
December 2024, the transition was 
implemented in phases, covering 
stakeholder alignment, capability 
building and on-ground execution, 
and was successfully completed by 
August 2025.
The initiative has delivered significant 
operational benefits. Critical issue 
resolution time improved from 
15 days to 1.7 days, while critical 
observations per DSS declined from 
1.22 to 0.19 across five CBM cycles. 
Distribution Transformer failure 
also reduced from 21 to 9 reflecting improved asset health and network 
reliability. Overall, the initiative has 
strengthened operational ownership, 
improved resource efficiency 
and enhanced service reliability, 
reinforcing our commitment to 
proactive asset management and 
operational excellence.

Lowered DT failures by 57%

Transmission
We transmit power from our gas-based 
generation plants to various offtake 
centres through 952 ckm of 400kV 
(including 720 ckm through Torrent 
Power Grid Limited - TPGL) and 388 
ckm of 220 kV. TPGL is a subsidiary in 
which we hold 90.25% and Power Grid 
Corporation of India Limited holds 9.75%. 
The existing transmission portfolio is 
governed by the CERC Tariff Regulations, 
delivering a post tax Return on Equity 
of 15.50%, along with applicable 
performance linked incentives.
In FY26, we expanded our transmission 
strategy by successfully commissioning 
transmission project at Khavda and 
progressing towards completion of 
transmission project at Solapur, marking 
a strategic step towards supporting 
large scale renewable integration, 
strengthening grid connectivity, and 
expanding the role of our transmission 
platform in India 's evolving power system.

Strengthening Testing Accuracy and Consumer Confidence
Continued investments in infrastructure and advanced testing capabilities have strengthened the accuracy 
and reliability of our metering operations.
The Meter Testing Laboratory at Ahmedabad has received renewed NABL accreditation (Certificate No. TC 
15800) for accuracy testing of smart meters, reaffirming compliance with national quality standards. The 
accreditation now covers smart meter testing as per IS 16444 (Part 1 & Part 2) and is valid for four years 
following the assessment conducted in February 2025.
This accreditation enhances assurance to utilities, consumers, and regulators regarding the 
precision, integrity, and consistency of smart meter testing, supporting reliable billing and transparent 
energy management.

Risk Management
Strengthening Stability in a 
Transforming Energy Landscape
In an evolving power sector, risks are dynamic and increasingly influence business models, 
investment decisions and stakeholder confidence. As this landscape evolves, we are 
strengthening our approach by integrating risk management into governance and decision-
making. This enables us to anticipate and mitigate risks, safeguard operations, support 
opportunities arising from the clean energy transition, and maintain resilience while protecting 
stakeholder interests.
Our Approach to Risk 
Management
Our approach is designed to ensure agility, 
alignment and continuous improvement in 
a rapidly evolving energy landscape:Forward-looking
Anticipating risks from energy transition,  
regulatory changes, technological and supply 
chain disruption, and climate imperatives
Integrated
Linking risk management with strategy, capital 
allocation, and operational priorities and risk 
impact–likelihood assessment (risk matrix)
Adaptive
Continuously refining frameworks in line with 
global best practices, industry benchmarks and 
evolving risk profiles
Risk-aware culture
Promoting organisation-wide awareness, 
accountability, and proactive management of risks

Risk Management Framework
Our framework combines structured processes, strong governance, and alignment with international standards to provide 
a comprehensive and enterprise-wide view of risks.
Focus
• We proactively identify risks to ensure operational 
stability and safeguard stakeholder interests.
• Risks are classified into Unit Risk, Industry Risk, 
and Macroeconomic risk, covering internal and 
external factors.Action
Identification of risks across generation, 
transmission, and distribution, such as fuel 
supply, grid failures, regulatory changes, 
renewable integration, Cyber security, demand 
variability, and climate events.01 Risk Identification
Focus
• Risk assessment is conducted to evaluate the potential 
impact of identified risks on achieving objectives.
• Risks are evaluated based on impact and likelihood, and 
are categorised as Low, Medium, or High.
• Mitigation strategies are developed with defined 
timelines to minimise disruptions.Action
Assessment of identified operational, financial, 
regulatory and safety risk, with mitigation through 
redundancy, fuel contracts, grid upgrades, 
cybersecurity, and regulatory coordination.02 Risk Assessment and Mitigation
Focus
• Identified risks and mitigation measures are 
documented, reviewed and updated in risk 
registers on quarterly basis.
• These records help in tracking risk evolution and 
improving response mechanisms.Action
Maintenance of a centralised risk register 
capturing asset-wise risks, with clearly defined 
ownership across key functions.03 Risk Registers
Focus
• Continuous monitoring of approved mitigation 
plans, with regular updates on execution progress.Action
Monitoring through industry-specific KRIs 
such as system losses, plant availability factor 
(PAF), renewable generation variability, Fuel 
price volatility, cyber incident alerts, regulatory 
developments, and safety incident trends.04 Risk Monitoring
Focus
• Top priority risks are identified and reported on 
periodic basis for informed decision-making.
• Any policy deviations, failures of existing control 
measures and other significant issues, if any, are 
also reported.Action
Structured reporting to Risk Management 
Committee, highlighting high-impact risks, 
compliance status with government regulations, 
and ESG expectations to support strategic 
investment decisions.05 Risk Review and Reporting

30.12.2024, the 362 MW

comply with SO2 emission 
norms or retire the plant by 
31.12.2030.

beyond the planned closure 
date, environmental 
compensation of ₹0.40/KWH 
will be applicable from January 
1, 2028.

developments and 
aligning operations within 
exemption timelines. R2. Financial Risk

not recognised in

Data Privacy and Cybersecurity 
Digital Resilience and 
Future-ready Operations
Cybersecurity and risk preparedness are central to T orrent Power's operations 
ensuring stability, continuity, and strong defence against evolving threats 
in a technology-driven industry. Through the adoption of advanced security 
frameworks, maintaining constant vigilance, and adherence to global best 
practices, we safeguard critical assets and uphold long-term trust in an 
interconnected world. This approach enables us to stay ahead in innovation, 
strengthen our teams, enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness, and 
deliver superior customer experiences.
Building Robust Cyber Resilience
Our commitment to digital advancement is matched by 
an equally strong commitment to securing it. Operational 
efficiency, customer experience, and innovation are each 
underpinned by a cybersecurity posture that evolves in step 
with technological progress.
Our IT systems holds ISO 27001:2022 certification under 
the Information Security Management System framework, 
aligning our practices with the most current global 
standards for information security, cybersecurity, and 
privacy protection.
Governance is anchored in our dedicated Cybersecurity 
Cell, which operates under the leadership of the Chief 
Information Security Officer (CISO). The Cell is responsible 
for cybersecurity governance, coordination, and 
strategic planning, while providing engineering support 
and continuously monitoring our risk posture through 
advanced processes and technology. We are in the 
process of establishing a 24/7 Security Operations Centre 
(SOC) that will enable real-time monitoring and response 
to cyber threats across the organisation. A Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP), sanctioned by the Ministry of 
Power, Government of India, is active across our Generation 
and Distribution businesses. Compliance with Central 
Electricity Authority (CEA)/CERT-In advisories is maintained 
rigorously, ensuring robust protocols are in place against 
suspicious domains.
Recognising the growing attack surface across IT and 
Operational Technology (OT) environments, we carried out 
comprehensive OT assessments at all unit locations. These 
assessments identified the gaps, thereby strengthening 
the ISO 27001:2022 certification for our OT systems. Our 
Vulnerability Management System operates on a proactive 
basis, identifying and addressing security weaknesses as 
they emerge, with structured reviews driving consistent 
tracking and timely remediation.

Advanced Audit Trail Implementation
We are one of the leading companies to implement an advanced audit trail mechanism that captures and stores changes 
at the database level, recording both pre-change and post-change values for critical financial records. This ensures 
complete traceability for transactions originating from both application interfaces and direct database interactions. The 
deployment of the Threat-Sense tool, aligned with MCA guidelines, further strengthens transparency, enhances control, 
and reinforces our commitment to regulatory compliance.
The following key initiatives reflect the breadth of our investment in strengthening digital defences. Together, these initiatives 
represent a structured and sustained effort, positioning Torrent Power to respond with confidence to an evolving cyber 
threat landscape.
Area Key initiatives

Governance•   Data Leakage Prevention (DLP), DPDP and Unified Endpoint Management (UEM): Implemented to 
safeguard sensitive information across endpoints, networks, web and email systems, in alignment with

•   User Access Right Review: Periodic review of user authorisations and permissions to ensure access 
remains appropriate and controlled. 
•   Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Extended across Microsoft Office 365 and application modules 
to strengthen identity verification.

and Cloud 
Security•   Next-Gen Antivirus and XDR: Deployed to detect anomalies, prevent lateral movement and contain

Building Awareness and Capability
Developing internal capability is as important as deploying

Information Security Management System (ISMS) awareness

A gap in visibility across external applications, networks,

security risks arising from external vendors and SaaS 
applications. To enable this, we have implemented a security 
solution using Vendor Risk Management (VRM) modules.

Generation
The generation business depends on advanced technology

Transformation

initiated the transition to S/4HANA to strengthen our 
enterprise technology backbone. This upgrade moves 
us from a highly customised legacy environment to 
a streamlined ‘Clean Core ' architecture, reducing 
technical complexity while enhancing system 
stability and scalability. Through the implementation 
of Multichannel Foundation for Utilities (MCFU) and 
Customer Engagement Manager (CEM), we are 
enabling seamless, digital-first customer experiences 
with enhanced self-service capabilities, while Fiori-
based applications empower our teams with a unified, 
360-degree view of customer interactions, improving 
responsiveness and decision-making. 
This transformation is helping us future-proof our 
operations, enabling greater agility, improved efficiency, 
and readiness to support a more sustainable and 
evolving energy landscape.Distribution
A broad range of digital and technological solutions has 
been deployed to strengthen our distribution network. The 
SCADA system provides oversight of all substations and 
feeders, while the integration of an Advanced Distribution 
Management System (ADMS) is under way to enable remote 
operations and network optimisation. Our automatic meter 
reading infrastructure, built on GPRS and NB-IoT technology, 
delivers real-time energy consumption data, and Advanced 
Metering Infrastructure (AMI) with Smart Meters is being

interface enhances functional efficiency and supports 
remote operations, and the mobile-based Field Force 
Application (FFA) enables field engineers to monitor activities 
and capture data digitally, improving operational efficiency 
and reducing reliance on paper-based processes.

to reduce cascading tripping risk and 
strengthen cyber preparedness.
A Power System Study for GNA 
covered reactive power management, 
dynamic system performance, 
harmonic analysis, electromagnetic 
transient behaviour, voltage unbalance 
and fluctuations, short-circuit level 
assessment, ferro-resonance risks, 
substation grounding, and end-to-
end protection coordination. This 
enabled identification and mitigation 
of system vulnerabilities, improved 
protection selectivity, and faster 
fault-clearing. We also built in-house 
capability through structured  training on industry-standard power 
system study software, reducing 
reliance on external consultants. 
Third-Party Protection Audits (TPPA) 
were conducted in line with WRPC 
and CEA guidelines at critical EHV 
substations. Following the Gujarat 
system disturbance on 12 March 2025, 
which resulted in significant load loss 
in the Western Region, the 400/132 
kV Pirana Substation was identified by 
WRPC for TPPA. A structured action 
plan was developed to address gaps 
in protection schemes, relay settings, 
and regulatory compliance, preventing 
mal-operations and reducing the risk 
of large-scale cascading outages.
We also pursued ISMS certification 
for our SCADA systems, identifying 
cyber vulnerabilities and implementing 
corrective controls to safeguard grid 
assets and ensure secure, resilient 
transmission operations amid evolving 
cyber threats.
Strengthening EHV Grid Resilience through System Studies, Protection 
Audits, and ISMS Certification

=== page 63 ===
Customer Service Enhancements
Customer experience is being progressively improved 
through a range of targeted initiatives. Mobile notifications 
for outages and updates, a mobile application, and 
a customer portal have been introduced alongside 
measures to improve billing accuracy and consumer 
satisfaction. Bill formats are being updated with QR codes 
to simplify payment, and multilingual AI chatbots are being 
implemented to deliver efficient, personalised customer 
service at scale.
Innovation and AI at Work
Open-source platforms and DevOps practices form 
the backbone of our IT application integration and 
delivery capability. Low-code/no-code platforms are 
used to accelerate application development, while the 
centralised deployment of Zabbix and OpenNMS provides 
comprehensive network monitoring and timely outage 
notifications. Microsoft Copilot has been integrated into 
daily operations to harness AI-driven efficiency, and our 
Enterprise Content Management System strengthens 
knowledge management and collaboration across the 
organisation. SAP Analytics Cloud and Power BI deliver 
robust data analysis and reporting capabilities.
By building on these technological foundations, we are well-
positioned to manage industry complexity, grow sustainably, 
and meet the country's increasing power demand.
Disaster Management and 
Business Continuity
A structured and tested recovery framework sits at 
the core of our approach to operational resilience. Our 
disaster management capabilities are designed to 
ensure the swift resumption of operations following any 
disruption, enabling rapid restoration of access to power, 
connectivity, data, hardware, software, and network 
equipment. The licensed distribution areas of Ahmedabad, 
Surat, and Dahej hold ISO 22301 (Business Continuity 
Management System) certification, a recognised 
standard that reflects the maturity of our business 
continuity framework.
Our Disaster Recovery infrastructure has been extended 
beyond the existing DR Site at Sify-Bangalore through the 
adoption of DRaaS (Disaster Recovery as a Service) from 
Microsoft Azure. This expands DR coverage for non-SAP 
applications, brings the benefits of cloud-based recovery 
services, and reduces dependency on the on-premises 
DR setup. Our framework integrates risk assessment, rapid response, 
and technology to strengthen operational resilience and 
ensure continuity during disasters. These capabilities enable 
us to remain prepared to safeguard our operations, support 
our people, and serve the communities around us across all 
forms of disruption.Continuity and Resilience Framework

Double Materiality Assessment
Turning Insights into 
Priorities
As a power utility navigating the dual pressures of India's energy transition and evolving 
global sustainability standards, we conducted a Double Materiality Assessment in this 
year to identify ESG topics with the greatest strategic relevance to our operations and 
long-term direction. The assessment evaluated each topic across two dimensions: its 
financial implications for the business, and its environmental and social impact. The 
insights gathered will guide how we mitigate risks, leverage opportunities, and shape  
our sustainability priorities going forward.

(CSRD) through E&Y. We reviewed the potential impacts, risks, and opportunities connected to each topic across both 
financial and impact dimensions, with the aim of strengthening our ability to align internal decision-making with stakeholder 
expectations around transparency, responsible conduct, and long-term value creation.

MT 6: Waste Management
Waste generation presents environmental and compliance 
risks across generation and operational sites. We manage 
waste through segregation, recycling and utilisation 
practices, targeting Zero Waste to Landfill (ZWTL) by 2028 and 
sustaining 100% fly ash utilisation. 
ST05 – Advance Responsible Actions
MT 3: Biodiversity Conservation and Habitat 
Management
Infrastructure development and operations may impact 
ecosystems and biodiversity across project sites 
and transmission corridors. We integrate biodiversity 
considerations into planning, minimise land disturbance, and 
undertake plantation and restoration initiatives.
ST05 – Advance Responsible Actions
MT 5: Operational Efficiency
Operational efficiency improves reliability, reduces losses 
and enhances cost competitiveness. We strengthen asset 
utilisation through process optimisation, loss reduction 
and digital interventions to improve network performance 
and returns. 
ST02 – Drive Operational Excellence
MT 11: Human Rights
Human rights risks arise if standards are not consistently 
upheld across workforce and value chain operations. We 
reinforce human rights principles through policies, employee 
training and supplier engagement. 
ST03 – Empower Stakeholders
MT 17: Business Ethics
Non-compliance with business ethics can affect reputation, 
stakeholder trust and regulatory standing. We reinforce ethical 
conduct through code of conduct requirements and reporting 
mechanisms to strengthen accountability.
ST02 – Drive Operational ExcellenceMT 19: Risk Management
Risk management strengthens resilience and operational 
continuity. We embed enterprise risk management across 
functions for proactive risk identification, mitigation 
and monitoring. 
ST02 – Drive Operational ExcellenceMT 12: Community Welfare
Community engagement supports inclusive development 
across operating regions. We implement focused initiatives in 
healthcare, education and social development to create long-
term community value.
ST03 – Empower Stakeholders
MT 4: Water Stewardship
Water dependence for thermal generation creates resource 
availability and regulatory risks. We optimise water use through 
efficiency measures, alternative sourcing and monitoring 
systems, targeting ≤2.2 m³/MWh (Coal generation) and ≤1.0 
m³/MWh (Gas generation) by FY2030.
ST05 – Advance Responsible Actions
MT 10: Customer Satisfaction and Loyalty
Customer satisfaction strengthens trust, service reliability 
and sustained demand. We enhance service delivery through 
quality standards, digital platforms and grievance redressal 
systems, maintaining >95% satisfaction and timely resolution. 
ST03 – Empower Stakeholders
MT 16: Corporate Governance
Inadequate oversight may impact compliance, transparency 
and decision-making. We strengthen governance through 
Board oversight, structured policies and ESG integration, 
including periodic Board-level ESG capacity building.
ST02 – Drive Operational Excellence
MT 18: Data Privacy and Information Security
Digitalisation increases exposure to cybersecurity and data 
privacy risks. We strengthen cybersecurity through system 
controls, assessments and role-based training, including annual 
Tier-1 vendor IT security evaluations. 
ST04 – Accelerate Digital TransformationMT 20: Economic Performance
Sustained economic performance supports growth, expansion 
and long-term stakeholder value. We focus on disciplined capital 
allocation, operational efficiency and portfolio optimisation to 
deliver consistent financial performance.

Strengthening Capital Management
We continue to follow a disciplined capital management approach that combines prudent debt optimisation, reinvestment and 
liquidity management. This ensures financial resilience while enabling us to fund expansion in line with our strategic priorities.
Over the years, we have consistently invested in expanding our renewable portfolio and strengthening our transmission and 
distribution network. During FY26, we allocated C 8,681  Crore towards capex, funded through a prudent mix of debt and internal 
accruals, while maintaining a strong focus on liquidity and long-term resilience. Alongside equity, we maintained our focus on 
prudent debt management.
Our Long-Term Debt-to-Equity ratio increased from 0.46 in FY25 to 0.67 in FY26, while our Net Debt-to-EBITDA increased from 
1.41 to 2.06, even-though with such increase in ratios, financial profile of the Company remains strong. The interest service 
coverage ratio stood at 6.17, ensuring ample liquidity. We continue to optimise our debt portfolio by balancing short-term and 
long-term borrowings, securing low-cost financing and pursuing refinancing opportunities.

=== page 78 ===
Strategic Allocation of Capital
In FY26, we invested ₹8,681 Crore in 
capital expenditure, underscoring our 
commitment to long-term growth and 
operational excellence. A significant 
portion was allocated to expanding 
our renewable portfolio, of ~₹6,010 
Crore, reinforcing our dedication 
to sustainability. The Company has 
raised long-term loans amounting 
to ₹6,420 Crore to support its 
strategic development and capital 
expansion initiatives.
We also prioritised strengthening our 
transmission infrastructure through 
strategic capital investments in key 
renewable energy evacuation projects. 
During the year, we commenced 
the Khavda transmission project in 
Gujarat for evacuation of power from 
a 4.5 GW renewable energy project, involving development of a 400 kV M/C 
transmission line (~60 km) along with 
bay upgradation, with an investment of 
~₹600 Crore. In parallel, we progressed 
the Solapur transmission project for 
evacuation of 1,500 MW of renewable 
energy, comprising a 400 kV D/C line 
(~40 Km) along with associated bays 
and substation infrastructure, with 
an estimated investment of ~₹500 
Crore. These investments reinforce our 
commitment to enabling large-scale 
renewable integration while enhancing 
network reliability and efficiency.
In addition, we undertook a strategic 
acquisition to support future thermal 
capacity, securing 100% ownership 
of Newzone India Private Limited, 
which holds 922 acres of land in close 
proximity to coal mines in Madhya Pradesh, and ~687 acres of land 
acquired and ~100 acres under process 
in Chhattisgarh for the development 
of the upcoming coal-based thermal 
power project, strengthening our 
project readiness and supporting 
diversified capacity expansion.

Aligning Employees with our Strategic Direction
Aligning our people with Torrent 
Power’s strategic direction is a 
deliberate and continuous endeavour. 
We articulate the Company’s mission, 
vision, and objectives clearly across 
all levels, enabling every employee to 
understand how their role contributes 
to our collective goals. A cascading 
strategy approach translates business-
level priorities into departmental and team-level targets, making the 
connection between daily work and 
organisational purpose tangible.
We reinforce this alignment 
through multiple communication 
channels—town halls, management 
circulars, intranet updates, and team 
discussions, ensuring that strategic 
priorities reach every corner of the organisation. Cross-functional teams 
work on shared objectives, enabling 
inter-departmental collaboration and 
better-informed decision-making. 
Performance evaluations are directly 
linked to strategic outcomes, ensuring 
that employee contributions are 
assessed in the context of what 
matters most to the Company.
Great Place to Work® 
Recognition
We have been certified as a Great Place to Work®,  
following the Voice of Torrent Employees (VOTE) 
Survey, which saw a strong 88% participation. Rooted 
in the belief that we listened and we acted—your 
VOICE matters, this recognition reflects the heart of 
our organisation—our people and the culture we have 
built—and validates a workplace founded on trust, 
respect, transparency and collaboration, shaped by 
independent and confidential employee feedback.
Guided by the spirit of Together Towards Tomorrow, 
we continue to strengthen a high-trust workplace 
built across key relationships and employee 
experience dimensions of credibility, respect, pride, camaraderie and fairness. These principles 
are embedded in how we work, lead and engage, 
reinforcing an environment where employees feel 
valued, inspired and proud to belong.
This recognition celebrates the passion and 
commitment demonstrated across teams and 
reinforces our deeply embedded Employee First 
philosophy and is in alignment with the Group’s core 
values. While this milestone affirms the strength of our 
culture and leadership approach, we view it as part of 
an ongoing journey—one that continues to guide us 
to listen, reflect and evolve as a unified team, further 
strengthening engagement and workplace practices.

Building Talent: Acquisition, Onboarding, and Early Development
A future-ready workforce begins with 
the right people in the right roles. Our 
talent acquisition strategy integrates 
structured recruitment practices, 
a compelling employer brand, and a 
seamless onboarding experience to 
attract, welcome, and retain high-
calibre professionals.
We evaluate candidates based on a 
combination of technical expertise, 
growth potential, and cultural 
alignment. Referral-driven hiring and 
unified recruitment drives allow us to 
access diverse talent pools efficiently. 
Our employer brand is built through 
authentic employee testimonials 
and a consistent presence on digital 
platforms, reinforcing Torrent Power’s 
reputation as an employer of choice.
Onboarding is designed to create 
immediate connection and confidence. New hires receive structured welcome 
communication, digital onboarding 
tools, and a dedicated induction 
programme that integrates them into 
our culture and operations from day 
one. Mentorship programmes and 
cross-functional introductions help 
them build professional relationships 
and settle into their roles with clarity 
and purpose.
Graduate Engineer Trainee 
(GET) Hiring & Onboarding 
Experience
We follow a centralised Graduate 
Engineer Trainee (GET) hiring process 
across all units, ensuring consistency 
in talent selection and strengthening 
our employer brand across leading 
engineering institutions. This unified 
approach enables us to attract high-potential talent aligned with our 
values, technical excellence and long-
term vision.
Our onboarding experience is 
continuously enhanced to support 
seamless integration and early 
engagement. Monthly New Joiners’ 
Meets provides a platform for 
interaction with senior HR leadership, 
enabling open dialogue, addressing 
queries and supporting a smooth 
transition into the organisation.
To build a strong cultural foundation, 
all new joiners are introduced to 
our legacy and values through ‘The 
Prescription’—a documentary on the 
life and vision of our founder, Shri U.N. 
Mehta. This initiative instils a sense of 
purpose, pride and belonging from the 
outset of the employee journey.Employees

CASE STUDY
Quality Week : Building Culture of Quality
Accountability for standards extends 
beyond individual performance 
evaluations. In FY26, our Renewable 
Energy division celebrated Quality 
Week across all renewable sites — 
wind, solar, hybrid, and centralised 
support locations achieving 100% 
participation. The programme was 
introduced to embed quality as 
a daily discipline, with objectives 
spanning first-time-right practices, 
risk prevention, standardisation, SOP 
adherence, and a zero-defect mindset.
Activities included toolbox talks and 
site briefings on quality standards; 
best practice sharing sessions 
showcasing case studies on defect elimination and predictive 
maintenance; quality quizzes and 
slogan competitions; site quality 
walks focusing on housekeeping, 
storage practices, documentation 
accuracy, and safety compliance; and 
refresher training on 5S, Root Cause 
Analysis, Kaizen, and Risk Mitigation, 
with emphasis on checklists, 
record maintenance, and inventory 
discipline. Across sites, teams have 
also reinforced 5S principles through 
visual installations created from scrap 
materials, such as Train, Elephant, and 
Horse models—which serve as creative 
reminders of workplace organisation 
and discipline. Participation spanned O&M teams, engineers, supervisors, 
and contract workers.
The outcomes were tangible: improved 
First Time Quality (FTQ) awareness, 
identification of improvement 
opportunities in equipment care and 
preventive maintenance, stronger 
cross-functional collaboration, and a 
heightened sense of ownership and 
accountability across teams. The 
division plans to conduct periodic 
cross-site quality audits, launch site-
level Kaizen projects, integrate quality 
KPIs into routine performance reviews, 
and establish Quality Week as an 
annual event.Fostering Well-being through Sports and Fitness
We promote employee well-being through initiatives such as marathons, walkathons and Khel-Mahotsav,

participation and fitness, Khel-Mahotsav provides an inclusive platform for employees and their families to 
engage together. This strengthens social bonding, enhances engagement and fosters a culture of health, 
teamwork and overall well-being.

Reliable power supply remains central to our 
customer commitment. During the year, we 
implemented targeted interventions to reduce 
disruptions and enhance network stability.
At the 132 kV Nicol-1 AIS Substation in Ahmedabad, 
a critical node in the network, a proactive initiative 
was undertaken to strengthen network resilience 
and ensure uninterrupted power supply. A first-
of-its-kind full topside overhead safety net was designed and installed across the switchyard using 
high-strength, UV-resistant material and corrosion-
resistant anchoring systems. Executed within a 
short timeframe, this solution effectively safeguards 
critical infrastructure from external disturbances, 
enhances operational safety and improves overall 
system reliability, while also serving as a scalable 
model for similar substations.

Our CSR Framework
We are committed to strong 
CSR governance to ensure the 
effectiveness, transparency, and 
accountability of our initiatives. At 
the Board level, the Corporate Social 
Responsibility and Sustainability 
(CSRS) Committee provides oversight 
of the Company’s community-facing 
programs. Our comprehensive and 
well-structured CSR Policy clearly 
defines our priority focus areas, 
project categories, programme types, 
implementation approaches, and 
resource allocation. This policy serves 
as a guiding framework for community 
engagement for all relevant employees 
and partners.
The CSRS Committee meets at least 
twice a year to formulate the Annual 
Action Plan (AAP), which outlines 
the selected projects, planned 
activities, and corresponding budgets 
for the year. Upon receiving Board 
approval, the Committee oversees 
the implementation of the AAP 
and periodically reviews progress 
and performance.Torrent Group is committed to inclusive community development by creating sustainable social, ethical, and environmental 
impact. Through our CSR initiatives implemented by the UNM Foundation, we focus on community healthcare, sanitation and 
hygiene, social care and concern as well as education and knowledge enhancement. Torrent supports underserved children 
through paediatric centres and speciality hospitals, promotes adolescent girls’ health and hygiene, strengthens public 
infrastructure, and advances education and skill development. These initiatives address local needs and improve quality of life, 
reinforcing the Group’s belief that strong communities are essential to long-term, sustainable growth.
Community Healthcare, 
Sanitation and Hygiene 
REACH ('Reach Each Child') is our flagship 
paediatric healthcare initiative launched 
in 2014 through the UNM Foundation, the 
philanthropic arm of the Torrent Group. The 
initiative is primarily directed at preventing 
child health problems through proactive 
grass-root interventions, focusing on 
children (six months to six years) and 
adolescent girls (11 to 18 years). The focus 
remains on improving early diagnosis, 
strengthening nutrition, enabling 
behavioural change, and ensuring access 
to specialised paediatric treatment across 
underserved regions of Gujarat.
Child Health Outreach
The outreach programme remains 
focused on strengthening preventive 
healthcare among children in underserved 
communities, with emphasis on early 
identification and timely management of 
malnutrition and anaemia. During the year, 
baseline screening camps were conducted 
at multiple villages in Gujarat, covering 
children aged six months to six years and 
enabling structured follow-up care.

Medical Services
UNM Children’s Hospital and PHCs
Our hub-and-spoke healthcare model 
is anchored by the 150-bedded NABH 
and NABL-certified UNM Children’s 
Hospital near Kamrej in Surat, which 
delivers advanced secondary and 
tertiary paediatric care, including 
complex surgical interventions. 
The hospital is supported by 11 
paediatric PHCs across Gujarat, 
providing outpatient care, diagnostics, 
medicines and referrals, enabling 
children in underserved communities 
to access timely medical services 
closer to their home. Access is further 
strengthened through free treatment 
for underprivileged families and 
subsidised care for others, ensuring 
equitable access to specialised 
healthcare. Since its inception in 2017, this integrated network has enabled 
thousands of underprivileged children 
to receive quality medical care, with the 
PHC network expanding further across 
underserved rural belts of Gujarat 
during the year.
Clinical capabilities continued to 
strengthen during the year, reflected in 
sustained growth in surgical capacity. 
In May 2025, the hospital achieved a 
milestone by completing 266 surgeries 
in a single month, surpassing the 
previous record of 210 surgeries set in 
July 2024. Our teams also undertook 
complex procedures, including a rare 
Caudal Duplication Syndrome case, 
while expanding developmental care 
for children with autism, intellectual 
disabilities and developmental delays through the newly inaugurated Child 
Neuro Development Centre, which 
offers physiotherapy and occupational 
therapy services.

Way Forward
Expanding Advance Paediatric and Neonatal 
Care
Building on the specialised paediatric healthcare capabilities, 
we are planning targeted upgrades to strengthen critical 
care infrastructure and neonatal support systems.
Critical Care Capacity
• PICU Upgrade (Level 2 → Level 3): Enhancing the unit’s 
ability to manage complex and critically ill paediatric 
cases through advanced monitoring and specialised 
treatment support
• NICU Upgrade (Level 3 → Level 4): Expanding capacity 
to treat extremely premature and high-risk newborns 
with advanced neonatal care facilities
Neonatal Nutrition Support
• Human Milk Bank: Establishment of a donor milk bank 
to provide safe, screened breast milk for premature 
and critically ill infants, supporting improved neonatal 
nutrition and reducing infection risksOutreach Expansion and Strategic Shift 
The programme will transition to a facility-led, demand-
driven model with an expanded focus on neuro paediatric 
care, alongside continued management of malnutrition and 
anaemia. Efforts will centre on early identification, referral 
and treatment of neurodevelopmental disorders through 
community awareness, village-level screening and caregiver 
training. Dedicated neuro care facilities will be established 
at select UNM Children PHCs, offering multidisciplinary 
interventions, including physiotherapy, occupational 
therapy, speech and behavioural therapy, special education 
and neuromodulation, to improve children ’s functional 
independence and social inclusion.
These enhancements will strengthen the hospital’s ability 
to deliver advanced paediatric and neonatal care, improve 
treatment outcomes for critically ill children and newborns, 
and expand access to specialised medical support for 
vulnerable infants.
Broadening the Continuum of Care
Alongside specialised paediatric care upgrades, the hospital is planning several initiatives to strengthen diagnostics, recovery 
support and operational resilience through rehabilitation centres, dialysis units, and hormone analysis capabilities, enabling 
more comprehensive care beyond the intensive care setting.

CASE STUDY
Triumph over the Rare
In	the	year,	UNM	Children	Hospital	
successfully performed a rare 
and highly complex paediatric 
urology	surgery	on	an	18	months-
old infant diagnosed with 
Caudal Duplication Syndrome—
an exceptionally uncommon 
congenital condition involving 
duplication of multiple pelvic and 
lower	abdominal	structures.	The	
infant presented with duplication 
of	key	organs,	including	the	
large	intestine,	urinary	bladder,	
urethra,	anal	canal,	vagina,	sacral	
bones	and 	external	genitalia,	
making it one of the rarest cases 
documented	in	medical	literature.The six-hour-long surgery was 
completed successfully without 
complications,	demonstrating	
the hospital 's advanced surgical 
expertise and strong clinical 
coordination.
This rare case was presented at 
the national level at the Society of 
Paediatric	Urology	conference,	
highlighting its clinical 
significance	and	academic	
contribution.	It	stands	as	a 	
milestone in UNM Children 
Hospital 's journey towards 
advancing specialised paediatric 
care and reinforces its capability 
to manage complex and 
rare	congenital	conditions,	while	
contributing valuable insights to 
the	global	medical	community.
CASE STUDY
Against All Odds: A Story of Survival and Strength
A critically premature baby born 
at	just	24	weeks	of	gestation 	
and	weighing	only	560	grams 	
was	admitted	to	the	UNM 	
Children	Hospital	NICU,	facing 	
life-threatening challenges from 
the	very	beginning.	With	severely 	
underdeveloped	lungs,	the	infant 	
required escalating respiratory 
support—from CPAP to intubation 
and mechanical ventilation—
along with surfactant therapy to 
sustain	breathing.	The	initial	days 	
were marked by intense medical 
intervention,	including	a 	cardiac	
arrest that required immediate 
CPR	and 	life-saving	medications, 	
followed by serious infections such 
as Candida in the endotracheal 
tube,	necessitating	aggressive 	
antifungal	treatment.	The	infant 	
also underwent multiple blood 
transfusions, 	phototherapy 	and	several critical procedures during 
this	period.
Supported by a highly skilled team of 
doctors,	nurses	and	advanced	NICU 	
infrastructure,	the	baby	gradually 	
stabilised.	Respiratory	support 	
was progressively reduced—from 
ventilator to CPAP and eventually to 
nasal	prongs—and	within	a 	week,	the 	
infant	was	breathing	independently. 	
Feeding	improved	steadily,	weight 	
gain	followed,	and	the	mother 	
was actively supported in gaining 
confidence	to	care	for	the	child.
After nearly three months of 
intensive	care,	the	baby	was 	
discharged as a neurologically intact 
survivor,	weighing	1.78	kg.	This 	
remarkable journey underscores the 
importance of advanced neonatal 
care,	multidisciplinary	expertise	and 	
sustained 	institutional 	support, 	
while reinforcing a powerful truth—
every	gram	matters,	every	breath 	
counts,	and	every	life	is	worth 	
the fight.

CASE STUDY
Healing Hands, Renewed Hope
An	eight-year-old	boy	was	admitted	with	a 	longstanding	non-union	(pseudarthrosis)	of	the	right	tibia,	a 	
condition	in	which	the	bone	had	failed	to	heal	properly,	significantly	affecting	mobility	and	quality	of	life.	
Following	detailed	evaluation,	surgical	intervention	was	undertaken	to	restore	structural	integrity	and	enable	
normal	function.	During	the	procedure,	both	the	tibia 	and	fibula 	were	carefully	osteotomised	and	realigned.	
Bone	grafts	were	harvested	 from	the	iliac	crest	as	well	as	the	tibia	to	stimulate	 healing.	 The	fibula	was	stabilised	
using	a	K-wire,	while	the	tibia 	was	fixed	with	a 	rush	pin	to	ensure	proper	alignment	and	stability.
The	surgery	aimed	to	achieve	solid	bone	union	and	restore	the	child’s	ability	to	walk	normally.	This case	
highlights	the	importance 	of	precise	surgical	planning,	advanced	orthopaedic	techniques	and	multidisciplinary	
care	in	managing	complex	paediatric	conditions,	ultimately	enabling	improved	mobility	and	a 	renewed	quality	of	
life	for	the	patient.
CASE STUDY
A Journey of First Steps
A	one-year-old	child	was	first	evaluated	in	July	2025	with	Global	Developmental	Delay	resulting	from	a 	perinatal	
insult.	At	the	time	of	initial	assessment,	she 	exhibited	significant	developmental	challenges,	including	absence	
of	head	control,	inability	to	sit	independently,	lack	of	standing	ability	and	limited	social	responsiveness,	with	
minimal	facial	expressions	and	difficulty	recognising	her	parents.
With	structured	intervention	through	physiotherapy,	she	began 	to	show	steady	and	encouraging	progress.	
Over	time,	she	achieved	the	ability	to	sit	independently	without	support	and	could	stand	with	assistance.	
Notable	improvements	were	also	observed	in	her	cognitive	and	social	development,	as	she	began	recognising	
familiar	faces	and	expressing	appropriate	emotions,	indicating	enhanced	engagement	with	her	surroundings.
Her	journey	reflects	the	impact	of	early	intervention,	multidisciplinary	care	and	sustained	therapeutic	support	
in	improving	developmental	outcomes.	It	stands	as	a 	testament	to	UNM	Children	Hospital’s	commitment	to	
delivering	compassionate,	specialised	paediatric	care	that	helps	every	child	move	towards	a 	healthier	and	more	
independent future.

Social Care and Concern for Environment 
Pratiti: Reviving Public Spaces for Greener Cities
City parks and public spaces have 
been facing ecological stress due to 
rapid urbanisation and the impact of 
climate change. These green spaces 
play an important role in controlling 
temperatures, improving air quality and 
biodiversity, collecting rainwater, and 
absorbing carbon and other pollutants, 
yet, many parks remain neglected. 
The Pratiti Programme was started 
as a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) 
between the UNM Foundation and local 
governing bodies to transform such 
spaces into sustainable ecological 
zones with areas for recreation, 
children’s play, pets, cultural events, 
and quiet reflection in natural 
surroundings.The programme is operational across 
Ahmedabad, Surat and Daman, with 
a total maintained area of ~2.39 lakh+ 
sq. mt. creating vibrant, inclusive 
public spaces that enhance greener 
community environment to live in, by 
providing leisure and recreation areas 
and improving the quality of life.
In Daman, Pratiti manages green 
stretches across Jampore Beach, 
Devka Beach, and Heritage spaces 
within the Daman Fort. Parks like Parimal 
Garden, Victoria Garden, Swati Park, 
Jyotindra Dave Garden in Ahmedabad 
and Surat are also maintained under 
Pratiti initiative to enhance biodiversity 
and sustaining multi-purpose public spaces aligned with the UN Sustainable 
Development Goals.

Environmental Strategy
At Torrent Power, environmental 
stewardship is integral to our 
operational philosophy and is 
guided by a robust Health, Safety 
& Environment (HSE) Policy. This 
policy underpins our commitment 
to minimising environmental impact, 
ensuring regulatory compliance and 
embedding sustainability into all 
aspects of our operations. It defines 
clear priorities, supports responsible 
decision-making and drives consistent 
environmental performance across our 
business. Majority of our operations 
are certified under ISO 14001:2015 
and ISO 50001: 2018, reflecting our 
structured and systematic approach to 
environmental management.
Our strategy is guided by a robust 
Environmental Management System 
(EMS) that improves operational 
efficiency while protecting the 
environment. We continuously monitor 
compliance status, track performance 
and implement corrective actions to 
drive ongoing improvement. Our key 
priorities include reducing greenhouse gas emissions, optimising energy 
and resource use, and managing 
water and waste responsibly. 
Aligned with evolving regulations 
and disclosure standards, we are 
strengthening our governance and 
climate responsiveness to reduce our 
carbon footprint, enhance resilience 
and support.
Advancing Low-carbon  
Energy Transition
We continue to advance our 
decarbonisation pathway towards 
a cleaner energy portfolio, with a 
clear focus on reducing greenhouse 
gas (GHG) emission intensity while 
maintaining reliable and efficient power 
supply. This is supported by operational 
efficiency, optimised fuel usage 
and a gradual shift towards cleaner 
energy sources.
Our gas-based generation fleet, 
supported by advanced combined 
cycle configurations, delivers lower 
emissions compared to conventional 
thermal generation while maintaining 
high efficiency and reliability. At the same time, we are improving the 
environmental performance of our 
thermal portfolio through adoption of 
ultra-supercritical technology in all new 
generations, enabling higher efficiency 
and lower specific CO₂ emissions. 
Looking ahead, we are also advancing 
our renewable energy and pumped 
storage project portfolio to enable 
greater integration of green power, 
support grid flexibility and build a more 
future-ready energy mix.
In our distribution business, we are 
further contributing through ongoing 
efforts to reduce T&D losses, improve 
system efficiency and expand rooftop 
solar adoption among customers, 
enabling them to participate more 
actively in the clean energy journey.
Our plants are designed for flexible 
operations to support renewable 
integration, supported by measures 
such as zero liquid discharge 
systems, high-efficiency electrostatic 
precipitators and continuous real-time 
monitoring of emissions and effluents 
to ensure responsible operations.

Water management is integrated into operational practices, with a focus on reducing freshwater dependency, increasing 
reuse and improving efficiency.
Regular monitoring of water consumption, along with internal and external water audits, awareness initiatives, and training 
programs on conservation practices, form the key pillars of our water stewardship. Accordingly, water conservation measures 
are planned and implemented.
Water use is optimised through process 
improvements such as ash pond water 
reuse, cooling system optimisation 
and efficient water handling. Recycling 
practices and system-level efficiencies 
help to reduce dependence on 
freshwater sources.
Water discharge is managed through 
treatment and reuse mechanisms.

and reuse of demineralised water and

Reducing Water Intensity through Efficient Use and Rainwater Harvesting
At our DGEN plant in Dahej 
(Bharuch,	Gujarat),	we	undertook 	
a focused water stewardship 
initiative to optimise water usage 
amid changing plant operations 
from round-the-clock to cyclic

CASE STUDY
Reutilising Aluminium 
Wire to Drive Cost 
Efficiency
As part of our continuous 
improvement and resource 
optimisation	efforts,	we	
implemented a Kaizen initiative 
across our Surat warehouse 
locations—Varachcha, 	
Vastadevdi,	Delhi	Gate	and	
Bhatar—to reduce material 
waste and improve cost 
efficiency.
Earlier,	cut	pieces	of	aluminium	
wire	(16	mm²	and	25	mm²),	
typically left over from 
temporary power supply 
setups,	were	routinely	
classified	as	scrap,	even	when	
usable lengths exceeded 
30	metres.	Recognising	the	
opportunity to minimise 
waste,	we	introduced	a 	revised	
process to re-deposit such 
cut pieces under their original 
material	codes,	enabling	their	
reuse	in	operations.
This	simple	yet	effective	
intervention has reduced 
unnecessary material 
procurement,	improved	
inventory utilisation and 
supported our sustainability 
goals	by	minimising	waste.
Achieved cost savings of  
~₹10 lakh in FY26

Strengthening Biodiversity and Sustainability Culture
We continue to strengthen our commitment to environmental stewardship by 
integrating biodiversity conservation, awareness and responsible practices into 
our operations. Our initiatives in plantation and green belt development across 
operational locations contribute to ecological balance and carbon sequestration.
Structured engagement with employees, communities and stakeholders reinforces 
environmental awareness. Through campaigns, outreach programmes and 
participation-led initiatives, we promote responsible practices and build a culture 
of sustainability across the organisation.
This culture is further strengthened through employee-led efforts, unit-level 
initiatives and community engagement, supported by communication platforms 
that extend awareness beyond our operation. Together, these integrated efforts 
enable us to enhance our environmental performance while supporting long-term 
sustainability and responsible growth.Driving Environmental Awareness through World

The initiative concluded with

reinforcing engagement and 
encouraging	continued	involvement.
Environmental Management and Certifications
At Torrent Power, environmental management is embedded within our operational 
framework through structured systems and continuous monitoring. Most of our 
plants are certified under ISO 14001 (Environmental Management System) and 
ISO 50001 (Energy Management System), reflecting our strong commitment to 
enhancing energy efficiency and reducing emissions, while demonstrating our

Members of the Company at the 1 9th Annual General 
Meeting held on August 10, 2023, had by way of special 
resolution accorded their consent to the Board of 
Directors to borrow from time to time such that the 
aggregate amount of borrowing outstanding at any 
point in time shall not exceed H 25,000 Crore (excluding 
temporary loans obtained from the Company’s 
bankers in the ordinary course of business), in such 
form, manner, and on such terms and conditions as 
the Board may deem fit including by way of term loans, 
debentures, bonds or other debt instruments, and to 
create charge, mortgage, hypothecation or security 
on the Company’s assets, both present and future, 
to secure such borrowings within the approved limits. 
The Members had further authorised delegation of 
these powers to Committee(s) of Directors, as may 
be required.
The Company operates in the Indian power sector, which 
is undergoing a multi-year structural transition requiring 
significant capital investment in renewable energy, 
thermal capacity, pumped storage, transmission, and 
distribution infrastructure. The Company’s current 
committed and under-construction pipeline includes 
approximately 4 GW of renewable energy projects 
across multiple locations, 1 .6 GW of thermal capacity 
greenfield project in Madhya Pradesh, and 3 GW of pumped storage projects in Maharashtra, in addition 
to ongoing network expansion and modernisation 
initiatives. These projects represent multi-year capital 
commitments to be funded through a combination of 
internal accruals and external borrowings aligned with 
execution timelines.
As on March 31, 2026, the Company’s total outstanding 
borrowings, including undrawn sanctioned limits, stood 
at approximately H 1 7 ,250 Crore. Based on the current 
committed capital expenditure pipeline and the recent 
acquisition of Nabha Power Limited, the Company 
expects borrowings to increase to approximately  
H 24,000 Crore over the near term. Accordingly, the 
existing borrowing limit of H 25,000 Crore is expected 
to be substantially utilised.
The Company anticipates incremental funding 
requirements arising from phased execution of its 
pipeline projects over the next 3-5 years. Accordingly, 
approval is sought to increase the borrowing limit from  
H 25,000 Crore to H 35,000 Crore. The revised 
limit provides a limited incremental headroom of 
approximately H 1 1,000 Crore aligned with project 
execution cycles.
The Company maintains a conservative capital 
structure with its current standalone Debt-to-Equity 
ratio at 0.85x, which may increase to approximately 
1 .70x (on FY26 financials) considering new borrowing 
limit. The Company’s credit ratings of ‘AA+/Stable’, as 
reaffirmed by rating agencies, continue to reflect its 
strong operational performance, diversified business 
portfolio, and prudent financial management. The 
rating agencies have factored in the Company’s capital 
expenditure programme and funding strategy and 
maintain a stable outlook.
The Company does not envisage any material change in 
its leverage policy as a result of the proposed increase 
and remains committed to maintaining a prudent capital 
structure. Borrowings will be undertaken in a phased 
manner aligned with the specific project funding
